newsitem.title: GERMANY: Five nabbed selling fake masterpieces in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Five nabbed selling fake masterpieces in Germany.

text.p: German customs investigators unveiled on Tuesday a collection of fake masterpieces which conmen tried to pass off as loot taken from Nazi Germany by the Red Army.
One of the 35 paintings and sketches supposedly by Renoir, Cezanne, Klee, Kandinsky and van Gogh was stamped as the property of top Nazi Hermann Goering to make the story more convincing.
The gang tried to sell the collection for $20 million, claiming they had been smuggled to Germany from Russia by way of Greece.
"They're really not very good and it doesn't take much expertise to realise they're fakes," one of the investigators told reporters shown the collection at a customs office in Munich.
Detectives posing as buyers arrested five suspects, one of them Greek. The paintings, believed to have been forged in Greece, will probably be destroyed after they are used in evidence.
Germany has been pressing Russia to return about 200,000 works of art taken as booty at the end of World War Two.
